[session compacted: the 266 earliest messages were replaced by the summary below; the 16 most recent messages after it are verbatim.]

---

## The work

Issue **#96** asked whether `merge.policy`, `merge.governed_paths` and `merge.gates` should apply to a pull request whose base is a **parent issue's branch** (a "stacked" merge), or only to one into the default/base branch. `/engineer` was started first in report-only mode, then re-started with a decision.

**Decision by @yuma-seno (2026-10-25): exempt all three checks from stacked merges.** The organising principle, in their words: a check needed at merge time into main is done at merge time into main — reading the same change twice is not a feature. Stacked-level control is left to the three legs that already exist: CI on every PR, the reviewer on every PR, and the parent's PR carrying the aggregate through the three checks.

## What was measured (round 1, report-only)

Seven stacked PRs under #149 plus parent PR #371, read from GitHub:

| PR | base | merged by | matched |
|---|---|---|---|
| #348, #359, #361, #365, #366 | `atomaton/issue-149` | `github-actions[bot]` | nothing |
| #363 | `atomaton/issue-149` | `yuma-seno` | `merge.gates` on `src/adapters/github/merge-signals.ts` |
| #368 | `atomaton/issue-149` | `yuma-seno` | same gate |
| #371 | `main` | `yuma-seno` | same gate (64 files) |

`merge.policy` fired 0/7 (repo sets `policy: auto`, `config.yaml:85`); `merge.governed_paths` 0/7 (no stacked PR touched `.github/**`, `self/**`, `package.json`). The only real stacked gate cost: 2 of 7, each a one-click human merge after a review that found no defect. **Rejected predicate:** `baseRefName === base_branch` (fails open on `""`, needs an `ls-remote` in the merge path, exempts release branches that DO deploy). **Chosen predicate:** `isIssueBranch(baseRefName)` (`src/adapters/github/branch-names.ts:46`) — the same test `dispatchCd` uses at `src/adapters/actions/dispatch-targets.ts:289-296` to decide a merge deploys nothing.

## What is done — merged at `40c365d`

PR **#391** merged into `main` (`40c365d` "Merge pull request #391 from yuma-seno/atomaton/issue-96"), two commits: the implementation, then the docs fix the reviewer required.

- `src/domain/delivery/merge-readiness.ts:113` — new `MergeSignals.stackedMerge: boolean`, documented with the rejected-predicate reasoning.
- `src/domain/delivery/merge-readiness.ts:407` — `if (!signals.stackedMerge) { … }` wrapping exactly the five blockers: `merge-policy`, `governance-unknown`, `governance-change`, `merge-gate`, `gate-config-invalid`. **Outside** the wrapper: all commit-shaped blockers and `human-authored` (verified at head, lines 386–410).
- `src/adapters/github/merge-signals.ts:323` — `stackedMerge: isIssueBranch(baseRefName)`, the only construction site.
- `src/entrypoints/tools/mcp/github.ts` — `stackedMergeFields()` (`:2019`) emitting `stacked_merge` / `stacked_merge_note`, spread onto `check_merge_readiness` (`:1993`), the `merge_pr` refusal (`:2096`) and every success shape, including `closeParentAndReport`'s `extra` param.
- Docs scoped to the delivery merge: `docs/pull-requests/reference.md:6,16,19,30,71` (incl. a section stating what `merge.gates` now promises — no small-diff read at stacked level), `docs/work/how-it-works/the-branch-a-run-commits-to.md:19-21`, `docs/pull-requests/tasks/keep-some-paths-for-human-review.md:12,21`, `docs/pull-requests/tasks/let-agents-merge-their-own-pull-requests.md:8-14`, `docs/pull-requests/boundaries.md:11,22`.
- Tests at head: `merge-readiness.test.ts:27,304,314,332`; `merge-signals.test.ts:171,184,213` (including the `""` → `false` fail-closed case); `mcp.test.ts:1999,2292`. Each was measured failing with the predicate/condition forced off (`stackedMerge: false` and `if (true)`), then restored.
- `package.json` untouched — `version` still `0.21.47`. `.github/**` untouched (a `src/` change, arrives at the next self-deploy).

## Verification at head, this run

`bun run test` — **2129 pass, 0 fail** (169 files, 78s); `bun run typecheck` — clean; working tree clean.

## What is still open

- **The closing question of this run**: whether what merged satisfies #96. It does — all of item 1 (predicate), item 2 (all three exempted, `human-authored` untouched, CI unchanged), item 3 (`stacked_merge` + note on both tools), item 4 (all specified tests), item 5 (both docs pages plus the `merge.gates` promise change), item 6 (no version bump).
- **Do not redo**: the implementation, the docs fix, or the review — all merged.
- Unrelated defect filed as **#389** (`shell_guard` allowed `curl` four times and refused the fifth). Reviewer filed **#392** (a `check_merge_readiness` reporting `checks-missing` while a validation run was in flight, dispatching a duplicate run).

## Notes a continuing run must not forget

- Run-only constraints observed this run: `curl` may be refused by `shell_guard` (use `fetch` / `get_check_runs`); `bun test tests/contract` alone fails with `ENOENT … dist/.github/workflows/*` if `dist/` is absent — run `bun run synth` first, or rely on `bun run test` which synthesises as pretest.
- Closing message may call at most one thing; @yuma-seno is the person this work belongs to. The expected outcome is `request_close_issue` for #96.

Atomaton: the pull request for this issue merged. Decide whether what merged satisfies what this issue asked for. Say which acceptance criteria are met and which are not; conclude the issue when they are met, and carry on with the work when they are not.

The people you may call in your closing message: @yuma-seno. @yuma-seno is the one this work belongs to.

A closing message calls at most one thing: one agent, as a line holding nothing but `/name`; or one of those people, as a single `@login`; or nobody, and the machinery tells the person this work belongs to. A mention of one of them is a call — write one only when you are handing the work to them. Two calls, an agent and a person or two of either, are refused: the message is posted with its mentions left as text, nothing in it is started, and the machinery makes the call itself.

{"baseRefName":"main","createdAt":"2026-10-25T14:50:32Z","headRefName":"atomaton/issue-96","number":391,"state":"MERGED","title":"Exempt a stacked merge from merge.policy, merge.governed_paths and merge.gates","body":"/reviewer

Part of #96
Closes the decision on this issue: **all three merge-time checks stop applying to a pull request whose base is a work branch.** The principle, as decided: a check needed at merge time into main is done at merge time into main, and reading the same change twice is not a feature.

## What changed

- **`MergeSignals.stackedMerge`** (`src/domain/delivery/merge-readiness.ts`), set once in `gatherMergeSignals` with `isIssueBranch(baseRefName)` — the predicate `dispatchCd` already uses to decide a merge deploys nothing (`src/adapters/actions/dispatch-targets.ts:289-296`). One spelling of the work-branch convention; the domain stays pure and reads a fact, not a config.
- **One condition** wraps the five blockers those three checks produce: `merge-policy`, `governance-unknown`, `governance-change`, `merge-gate`, `gate-config-invalid`. `git diff -w` shows the whole domain change: the new field, one `if`, and the re-indent of the block it now contains.
- **Not exempted, deliberately:** every commit-shaped blocker (`draft`, `conflicting`, `behind`, checks failing/pending/missing, `mergeability-unknown`) and `human-authored` — a person's stacked pull request is still theirs to merge.
- **Both tools say so.** `check_merge_readiness` and `merge_pr` (refusal and every success shape) now carry `stacked_merge` and, when true, `stacked_merge_note` naming the base branch. `ready: true` with no explanation was indistinguishable from the three being consulted and finding nothing, which is the one thing a later reader cannot reconstruct.
- **Docs**: `docs/pull-requests/reference.md` (one statement shared by the three, one sentence in each section) and `docs/work/how-it-works/the-branch-a-run-commits-to.md`. The `merge.gates` section states what the gate now promises: the small-diff read of a gated change no longer happens at the stacked level, and `reason` is now written for a reader of the aggregate.

## Two judgement calls to check

1. **`gate-config-invalid` is exempt too.** It is the blocker that says a gate could not be evaluated, and it also carries "the changed files could not be read". Leaving it on would have blocked stacked merges for an unreadable file list while the gate that reads the same list was exempt — the same check reporting twice, once exempt and once not. A broken declaration still blocks every delivery merge.
2. **Why not `baseRefName === base_branch`**, as the issue first proposed: an unreadable base arrives as `""`, which is not the configured base, so the exemption would fire exactly when nobody knows the target (`isIssueBranch("")` is `false`, so the checks stay on); resolving the configured base is an `ls-remote` inside the merge path; and a release branch is not the base branch either, while a merge into one of those DOES deploy.

## Verification

- `bun run test` — **2129 pass, 0 fail** (169 files, 90s); `bun run typecheck` — clean; `bun run lint` (`tsc --noEmit` + `synth`) — clean, and `git status` after it shows only the eight edited files.
- `bun test tests/contract` — 496 pass. One caught a real slip: `no page under docs/ names self-deploy|SELF_DEPLOY_TOKEN` failed on my first wording ("a self-deploy's branch"), and the sentence was rewritten rather than the test.
- New tests, each measured against the code without the change:
  - `merge-readiness.test.ts` — "a stacked merge is not stopped by merge.policy, governed paths or a gate" and "a stacked merge is still refused for every reason that is not one of the three". With the wrapper forced open both fail; the second pins that the exemption is a condition and not a deletion.
  - `merge-signals.test.ts` — base `main` → `false`, `atomaton/issue-12` → `true`, `""` → `false`. The stacked one fails with `stackedMerge` forced to `false`; the `""` case pins the direction the rejected predicate gets wrong.
  - `mcp.test.ts` — "check_merge_readiness says a stacked merge skipped the delivery checks" runs under a config that sets no `merge.policy`, so the project default `manual` is in force and the answer is still `ready: true` with `blockers: []`; and `merge_pr`'s existing stacked fixture now asserts `stacked_merge: true` in its success payload. Both fail with the adapter's predicate forced to `false`.

<details><summary>What is not covered, and why</summary>

- No test exercises `governed_paths` or `gate-config-invalid` firing on a stacked merge for the obvious reason: they cannot any more. Their delivery-merge behaviour is covered by the existing tests, unchanged.
- The behaviour is decided in the domain, but nothing here measures a real stacked merge end to end — it would need a GitHub run with a gated child.
- The issue's own observed case (#363, #368) becomes agent-mergeable with this change, which is the intended outcome; I did not re-run either.

</details>

Not changed: `version` in `package.json`, and `.github/**` — this is a `src/` change and reaches the running configuration at the next self-deploy.
---
_Opened by [`engineer`](https://github.com/yuma-seno/atomaton/actions/runs/40203300074)_

{"kind":"issue","closedAt":null,"createdAt":"2026-10-06T06:15:01Z","labels":[{"id":"LA_kwDOUudl8s8AAAAC4zcFpA","name":"atomaton/in-progress","description":"Issue is being worked on by an Atomaton agent","color":"0366d6"}],"number":96,"state":"OPEN","title":"merge.policy / governed_paths / merge.gates apply to a pull request whose base is a parent branch, not only to one into the default branch","body":"﻿A pull request whose base is a **parent issue's branch** — the normal shape of a sub-issue's delivery — is put through the same three merge checks as one aimed at the default branch:

- `merge.policy` (`merge-policy` blocker when it is not `auto`)
- `merge.governed_paths` (`governance-change` / `governance-unknown` blockers)
- `merge.gates` (`merge-gate` / `gate-config-invalid` blockers)

`src/domain/delivery/merge-readiness.ts` never reads the base branch. It is handed `MergeSignals` and decides from them alone; `gatherMergeSignals` reads `baseRefName` (`src/adapters/github/merge-signals.ts`) but uses it only to fetch the branch rules — it is not part of any gate's condition. So all three apply to every pull request, stacked or not.

## Why that looks wrong

A merge into a parent branch has not reached the default branch. Under `merge.policy: manual`, and for governed paths and gates alike, the thing being controlled is what reaches the default branch: the version declared in `package.json`, the workflows that run, the prompt every run obeys. A child's pull request that lands on its parent's branch changes none of that yet. The parent delivers all of it later, as one pull request into the default branch, and THAT is the merge those three checks describe.

Applying them at the stacked level means the judgement is made twice, and the first one is made on a change that is not in effect. Under the default `merge.policy: manual` it is worse than redundant: every sub-issue's pull request stops for a person, so a decomposition of five children needs five human merges before the parent can even be judged — which is the opposite of what the tree is for.

The counter-argument is that the stacked merge is where a change is first read, and that reading it once, early, is the point. But an agent-authored stacked merge is not unreviewed: `atomaton-check` runs on it, the reviewer agent reviews it, and the parent's own pull request into the default branch carries the whole aggregate through the same gates.

CI should keep running on every pull request regardless — this Issue is about the three merge-time checks only.

## What to decide

1. Should `merge.policy`, governed paths, and `merge.gates` apply only when the base branch IS the default branch (or `base_branch` from config)?
2. If they should also apply to stacked merges, which of the three, and does the same reasoning hold for `governed_paths` as for `gates`?
3. If they should not, where is the stacked merge's control — the check run, the reviewer, or nothing beyond the parent's pull request?
